arguments.conclusion: Gold is crashing because a liquidity crisis forces holders to sell gold for liquidity, rather than due to fundamental bearishness on gold, serving as a specific instance of the broader economic downturn risk from the Strait of Hormuz conflict.
source_speech_filenames: 20260327_Why is Gold Crashing from the War.txt
arguments.premise_synthesis: During a liquidity crisis, investors sell what they can sell, not what they want to sell. In the current conflict, almost all assets have sold off: gold down 25%, silver down, S&P down, TLT down 5%. Gold is a global reserve asset, so it is one of the first things sold for liquidity. This indicates the gold crash is liquidity-driven.
arguments.conclusion_supported: The gold crash is a result of a liquidity crisis triggered by the Strait of Hormuz conflict, consistent with the CC that the economy faces high risk and gold crash via liquidity crisis.
